overview: The Medford Historical Commission held public hearings on several properties subject to the demolition delay ordinance and met with Building Commissioner Bill Forte to discuss legal authority and ordinance revisions. The Commission designated properties at 91 Winchester Street and 17 Green Road as preferably preserved, approved releasing the demolition delay for 28 Grove Street, and authorized funding for a historic inventory survey of 37 Locust Street.

items.title: Preferably Preserved Hearing: 91 Winchester Street
items.summary: The Commission voted to find the carriage house at 91 Winchester Street preferably preserved after reviewing its architectural significance and discussing structural safety concerns with the homeowner and Building Commissioner.

items.title: Preferably Preserved Hearing: 17 Green Road
items.summary: The Commission voted to find 17 Green Road preferably preserved while agreeing to convene a subcommittee meeting to review proposed addition and porch restoration plans.

items.title: Demolition Review: 142 Mystic Avenue
items.summary: The Commission voted to pass on historic significance review for 142 Mystic Avenue because permit records established the structure was built in 1949 and does not meet the 75-year age threshold.

items.title: Demolition Application and Survey Request: 37 Locust Street
items.summary: The Commission accepted the full demolition application for 37 Locust Street contingent on receiving a site plan within 10 days, and voted to allocate $500 for a Massachusetts Historical Commission Form B survey.

items.title: Demolition Delay Review: 28 Grove Street
items.summary: The Commission voted to release the demolition delay for 28 Grove Street following review and approval of revised architectural drawings for the exterior alterations.

items.title: Discussion on Ordinance Enforcement with Building Commissioner
items.summary: Building Commissioner Bill Forte presented recommendations regarding legal authority, ordinance language, demolition delay durations, and potential mitigation fee structures, and the Commission agreed to consult city legal counsel.

items.title: Site Plan Review and Community Events
items.summary: Commissioners noted a site plan review filing for 285-295 Middlesex Avenue and announced an upcoming June 1 public presentation at the library on a local World War II veteran memorial.

items.title: Project Updates and Approval of Minutes
items.summary: The Commission reviewed progress on CPA-funded masonry repairs at Thomas Brooks Park and Pomp's Wall, discussed future historical marker planning, and approved the April 2023 meeting minutes.
